question: GQ-004
action: built the want-list generator — the gap I named four loops running without closing

output.contract_fields: all 7 present (identifier, title, year, language, tier, rights_evidence, query)

why_106_not_124.cause: The census deduped candidates against the LIBRARY but not against each other. Cookery fetched 60 results containing only 56 unique titles — 4 intra-pool duplicates. The generator dedupes both ways, plus cross-subject (a book can carry several subjects).
why_106_not_124.consequence: My census overcounted by ~18. 106 is the number of distinct fetchable works.

correcting_last_loop: I wrote that only science fiction had duplicate titles, 5 of 6 pools at zero. Cookery has 4. My duplicate check compared numFound to unique titles in the SAMPLE I had fetched; for five subjects that sample was the full pool, but I read "0 duplicates" as a property of the pool rather than of my comparison. Fourth over-generalisation, same shape, caught by building on it.

rights_flag.decision: Flagged in the file, NOT removed. They carry IA's explicit rights field, which is the contract's evidence, and removing them would be a copyright judgement I have consistently declined to make. A reviewer can check seven items rather than 106.

still_not_ingested: This produces a want-list. Fetching and ingesting is a separate step the adapter owns.
